subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should OpenClaw define a native context-pressure alert and recovery contract for terminal `done` sessions, and which threshold, surface, and recovery action should own it?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the signal exists but no current product contract says when saturated terminal sessions should alert or recover, so implementation would otherwise bake in policy choices.

options.title: Add Observe-First Context Pressure Diagnostics
options.body: Add a session context-pressure classification that covers active and terminal rows and surfaces operator-visible warnings before any automatic cleanup.

options.title: Add Automatic Recovery Semantics
options.body: Define thresholds and recovery actions that can clean up or restart saturated terminal sessions, with stronger live proof and rollback controls.

options.title: Keep Status-Only Visibility
options.body: Decline native alerting for now and document that operators must inspect session context usage manually or through external monitoring.

recommendation.title: Add Observe-First Context Pressure Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add a session context-pressure classification that covers active and terminal rows and surfaces operator-visible warnings before any automatic cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The current diagnostic heartbeat and health/session summary paths route most directly through recent history attributed to steipete in this checkout.
